title: Evo genomic language model designs functional toxin-antitoxin and anti-CRISPR systems
summary: Evo used genomic context to generate functional bacterial defence-system components. The paper reports an AI-generated toxin and low-sequence-similarity antitoxins that neutralized it in growth assays, including antitoxins that also acted against multiple natural toxins; it also reports five generated anti-CRISPR proteins that protected bacteria against Cas9 activity in cell and phage assays. Two generated anti-CRISPR proteins lacked significant sequence similarity to known proteins. These experiments demonstrate function-guided genomic design beyond simple copying of natural sequences.
ai_technology: Evo 1.5, a long-context generative genomic language model trained on prokaryotic DNA sequences

evidence.tested: The paper reports an AI-generated toxin and low-sequence-similarity antitoxins that neutralized it in growth assays, including antitoxins that also acted against multiple natural toxins; it also reports five generated anti-CRISPR proteins that protected bacteria against Cas9 activity in cell and phage assays.
evidence.unknown: This is a set of functional in-vitro bacterial assays, not evidence of therapeutic use, broad host range or ecological performance. One generated toxin had 71% sequence identity to a known RelE toxin; novelty is especially supported by low-similarity antitoxins and anti-CRISPRs, two of which lacked significant sequence identity to known proteins. Earlier Evo phage-genome design and Evo 2 regulatory-sequence work are different papers and different functional results; this row is limited to the toxin-antitoxin/anti-CRISPR findings in the cited Nature article.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers prompted Evo 1.5 with genomic contexts that associate functionally related bacterial genes and used it to generate candidate toxin-antitoxin and anti-CRISPR sequences. Candidates were filtered computationally, synthesized/expressed and tested in bacterial growth, Cas9-protection and phage assays. AI generated candidates; the biological activity was established experimentally.
